newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM backs Renault unions proposals.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM backs Renault unions proposals.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene on Tuesday urged Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer to seriously consider trade union proposals on keeping the French car maker's Belgian plant open.
In a letter to Schweitzer, Dehaene asked him to "examine and discuss workers' proposals with very much attention".
Schweitzer and workers and management of the plant in Vilvoorde near Brussels are due to meet in Beauvais, France, at 1400 GMT on Wednesday.
Dehaene said the unions proposed to keep Vilvoorde open, after a restructuring, for a transitional period of two to three years during which a final solution could be worked out.
He said that early retirement and shorter working weeks with reduction of social charges for employers could be applied in the restructuring.
Dehaene noted he had already proposed the latter in an earlier letter to Schweitzer on March 13.
Renault decided on February 27 to close the Vilvoorde plant in July with a loss of 3,100 jobs.
